act36side.png.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: a finished portrait cover image for an Arknights visual novel library.
Input image 1: the original Delicious on Terra event banner, the subject and artwork source.
Input image 2: an official Near Light archive cover, a reference ONLY for the layered archival-card construction, proportions, frame, reel, and type hierarchy.
Create our own cover for Delicious on Terra using image 1 as the central illustration. Preserve its four recognizable travelers, faces, clothing, poses and pale ruined city artwork as faithfully as possible; treat the banner as a printed picture insert. Make the ensemble fit inside a clean off-white photograph border. Build a compact portrait archival collage around it with dark desaturated backing paper, a small film reel, and restrained gold and pale sage accents derived from the Delicious on Terra artwork. A dim cropped echo of the same illustration may appear behind the photo, but do not invent additional characters. The overall card should visually belong beside image 2 without reusing Near Light content, its skyline, branding or red/blue palette.
Text verbatim: "DELICIOUS ON TERRA", prominently legible in a tasteful gold fantasy display title below the illustration. Only this title; no extra labels, numbers or microtext. Use a coherent original layout, not a copy of another website's cover.
Output: one standalone high quality portrait raster cover, approximately 5:6 proportions, the entire card visible with modest transparent padding around its irregular paper silhouette. Genuinely transparent outside the card. No scene mockup, no watermark. Preserve the supplied illustration instead of reimagining the characters.

edits.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the current generated Arknights cover.
Input image 2 is an OFFICIAL REFERENCE ONLY for the small white recording-tape reel/spool on that cover.
Make a narrowly targeted correction to image 1, preserving everything else:
1. Replace its large vintage metal cinema reel with the same type of flat white recording-tape reel seen in image 2. Closely match the reference object's white circular face, three broad black radial sections spaced 120 degrees apart, small dark gray/black center hub, and understated flat graphic style. It should resemble the reference's clean white disc, NOT a bronze/steel movie-projector reel with open triangular holes or numerous spokes. Include exactly ONE reel and keep it at the target's current reel location. Keep it modest in size, like the official cover.
2. Remove ALL loose tape, curled film, loops of tape, perforated filmstrips, and strips of adhesive/masking tape throughout the target. No filmstrip sprocket holes, no trails of film attached to the reel. Where these objects were, restore the nearby plain backing paper or transparent exterior as appropriate. A picture that was framed as a filmstrip can remain as a plain photo without perforations. Do not substitute new objects.
Invariants: preserve the central illustration, every character's face and pose, photograph border and angle, title wording and typography, color palette, remaining paper layering, and other non-tape decorative motifs. Do not redraw or redesign the main artwork. Preserve the target's overall portrait aspect ratio, framing and transparent exterior. The input 2 story artwork, title and other decorative objects must NOT be imported.
Output: the complete edited cover alone, same composition and portrait proportions as input 1, genuine transparent background, no mockup, no extra text, no watermark.
Target: Delicious on Terra. Keep the gold "DELICIOUS ON TERRA" title banner and its emblem intact, and keep the travelers exactly as shown. Correct the reel at the upper right. Remove the looping film along the right edge, perforated filmstrips at the top and lower right, and the green adhesive strip/tab near the top; retain the actual leaves, flowers and plain paper photographs. The gold banner bearing the title is not tape and must remain.
